author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Palestinians in Qaryut, south of Nablus in the occupied West Bank, say increasing Israeli settler attacks and military restrictions are making life increasingly dangerous and forcing families to leave.

The village is surrounded by at least seven illegal Israeli settlements and outposts. 

Residents say settlers are taking over more land and threatening Palestinian families, while Israeli soldiers prevent some farmers from accessing their olive groves. 

In March, two Palestinian brothers were killed by Israeli settlers near their home, and the attackers remain free, according to the report.

Qaryut lies in Area B, which is under partial Palestinian control while Israel retains security control. Residents say this status offers them little protection.

Dozens of families have already been forced to leave the village. Palestinians say Israeli authorities and settlers are creating a coercive environment aimed at driving them from their land.

Al Jazeera’s Nida Ibrahim reports from Qaryu

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
The UK government has announced plans to triple the number of data centres to meet growing demand for artificial intelligence. But as large parts of the country face unprecedented heat and drought, questions are being raised about how much water and electricity these facilities consume.

Data centres generate significant heat and require cooling, with some facilities relying on large amounts of water. In England, the industry is more regulated, with many facilities using closed-loop systems that consume less water while still requiring substantial electricity.

As AI drives rapid expansion, the search is on for more sustainable solutions. At a data centre in London’s Docklands, Digital Realty is using river water to cool its systems before returning it, as the industry looks for ways to reduce its environmental impact.

But data centres are expanding faster than renewable resources can be delivered, while rising temperatures and drought add to the challenge.

description:
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has announced plans to isolate Iran's economy through targeted measures to be revealed on Monday, saying the new actions could reduce the need for further military action. 
Bessent warned US allies: "You're either with us or against us," saying Washington would use its "full might and force" against countries doing business with Iran. 
Tehran dismissed the threats, with Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi calling the so-called "economic D-Day" a "diversion from America's own crisis." 
In an interview with Al Jazeera, Professor Mostafa Khoshcheshm of the University of Applied Sciences and Technology in Tehran said US economic pressure would not work, noting that similar sanctions have been imposed for 15-16 years. 
He said Bessent had offered only "vague words" without specifying new sanctions laws, sectors or entities, and argued that "threatening is Donald Trump's method."

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
An investigation into the death of former White Helmets volunteer Mohammad Ghamira in police custody in Syria has found no evidence of deliberate physical abuse, officials say. Ghamira, who had haemophilia, died from a brain haemorrhage after being detained in al-Haffah over a financial dispute. Witnesses told investigators that a police officer slapped him despite authorities being warned about his condition. The officer has been detained and referred for prosecution. Ghamira's death has sparked anger and protests, reviving painful memories of torture and abuse in detention under the Assad regime. Rights groups say they have received testimony of other cases of alleged abuse and deaths in custody, while Syria's Interior Ministry says it is restructuring its security forces and strengthening human rights training.

Al Jazeera's Heidi Pett reports from al-Haffah, Syria.
